cases.title: Panel: Show me again explains the change already made with a frame, and makes no second demonstration

rubric.reason: Turn 4 ran preview_frame, changed nothing, explained the one change in plain words ("Title's Position from 0.5 to 1.5 s now gets up to speed early and spends most of the move slowing down"), and handed back the rest in one sentence ("The other three moves are yours").

Every name and time, such as Title's Position 0.5 to 1.5 s and 3 to 4.37 s, Old Take, CTRL, Icon, Logo's Rotation, Subtitle's Opacity, Bar's X Position and Glow's Blurriness, matches the tool output, and Turn 4's "fastest part is near the start" follows from the check's fastest "first".

Each turn stays short and ends with something for the learner to do; Turn 3's demo hands back "the other three moves" in one sentence, and Turn 4, setting aside the blank-frame remark, gives the explanation, a brief way to see it, and the pending step ("say done").

Turn 4 ran preview_frame, made no change or second demo, explained the existing shape in words ("the ease out of the first key is short and the ease into the 1.5 s key is long"), and handed back the remaining pairs in one sentence ending "say done".

Turn 4's names and times (Title's Position 0.5 to 1.5 s, 1.5 to 3 s, 3 to 4.37 s, Scale, and 0.8 s) all match the snapshot, check and preview_frame results, and "near the start" follows from the check's fastest "first".

Setting aside the blank-frame remark, Turn 4 moves one idea, the shape already made on Title's Position, in a sentence and ends by handing over the task: "a short ease out and a long ease in, and say done."

Turn 4 calls only preview_frame, explains the existing change in words without influence numbers ("leaves its 0.5 s key after only a short ease and spends most of the move slowing into its 1.5 s key"), says "I didn't change anything this time", and hands back the other three in one sentence ending "say done".

Every name and time the mentor uses, such as Title's Position 0.5 to 1.5 s, 1.5 to 3 s, 3 to 4.37 s (rounded from 4.367), Scale, Old Take, CTRL, Icon, Logo's Rotation, Subtitle's Opacity, Bar's X Position and Glow's Blurriness, matches the speed_graph_snapshot, speed_graph_demo or preview_frame output.

Each turn moves one step and ends with something to do or answer: the land-hard question in turn 1, the fastest-point question in turn 2, and "say done" after the demo in turn 3 and the single explanation in turn 4, with the blank-frame remark ignored as a fixture artifact.
